title: conntrack namespace leak causing cross-tenant traffic on Dedicated hosts
creator: Aisha Karim
description: Multiple Dedicated customers reported sporadic cross-tenant connections and misrouted traffic during VPC peering tests and live traffic bursts. Symptoms included unexpected TCP connection reuse between tenant workloads, intermittent DNS resolutions pointing to wrong tenant endpoints, and transient policy violations in packet capture. This ticket tracks the investigation, root cause, fix, rollout, and customer communications.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two Dedicated tenants A and B on the same host pool with tenant-level VPC peering to customer on-prem networks.
2) Configure one workload in tenant A to open many short-lived outbound connections to a NATed external IP while tenant B opens outbound to a different external IP.
3) Observe conntrack table and packet captures on the host during bursts.
4) Reproduce with host-networked inference workers under high connection churn.
Expected: No cross-tenant conntrack entries or misrouted flows.
Observed: conntrack entries with mismatched tenant labels and socket reuse across namespaces under high churn when host NAT path is used.
investigation_notes:
- Initial report from Customer X (Priority enterprise) showed cross-tenant latency spikes and occasional request failure with 403 where RBAC logs indicated the request originated from another tenant.
- Captured conntrack snapshots and pcap from affected host: found 10-20 conntrack tuples where source IP/port pairing was reused with a different netns id than the originating workload.
- Network agent (netd) logging correlated NAT translation path with a shared iptables chain that runs in the host namespace.
- Reproduced locally by running two network namespaces and stress-testing with many ephemeral TCP connections; conntrack table entries got associated with the host conntrack table instead of per-tenant namespace under certain race conditions during veth teardown.
- Investigated kernel config and found conntrack table access was shared when using legacy iptables + host-based NAT in our current deployment mode for Dedicated.
- DNS anomalies were secondary: long TTL negative caching in in-host DNS proxy combined with incorrect src NAT resulted in lookups resolving to a peered route that belonged to the wrong tenant when entries leaked.
root_cause: A race in the Dedicated host networking path where ephemeral veth teardown and reuse interacted with host-level conntrack/NAT chains. When workloads used host-NAT path for egress (our optimizer for throughput), conntrack tuples were inserted into shared tables and retained when veths were removed, allowing subsequent flows from another tenant to match and reuse NAT translations. Coupled with aggressive DNS caching in the host DNS forwarder, this caused transient cross-tenant routing and perceived isolation failures.
resolution:
1) Implement kernel-level mitigation: pin conntrack table entries to network namespace by ensuring conntrack is used in the per-namespace nf_conntrack instance (enable pernet_namespace_conntrack and ensure netfilter modules load per-netns).
2) Short-term hotfix: modify netd to create a tenant-specific conntrack mark (CONNMARK) and add iptables rules to clear/mask conntrack entries when tearing down a tenant veth so stale entries are not matched by other tenants.
3) Adjust DNS proxy to respect tenant-specific cache namespaces (split DNS cache) and reduce negative TTL to 30s for peered routes.
4) Add guardrail: disallow host-NAT egress optimization for tenants with VPC peering enabled until kernel-level fix is deployed.
5) Backported patch into runtime-2.4.1 and staged in canary pool for validation.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (hotfix) - immediate: deploy netd change + iptables connmark rules to canary hosts (canary size: 2 host pools) and monitor for 24h. Notify impacted customers and enable temporary guardrail to disable host-NAT optimization for their tenants.
Phase 2 (kernel/arch) - medium term: coordinate with infra to enable per-namespace conntrack and roll kernel module changes across Dedicated host images. Target window: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 - final: re-enable host-NAT optimization after verification and increase canary to 20% then full fleet.
Rollback: revert netd change and restore previous iptables chain if regressions within 2 hours of deploy. Automated rollback hook present in deployment pipeline.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for netd connmark logic and iptables rule generator.
- Integration tests: simulated tenant churn in CI using network namespaces, verifying no cross-namespace conntrack matches under high connection churn.
- E2E: deploy to canary hosts and run Customer X traffic replay harness for 48h.
- Post-deploy probes: periodic conntrack dumps + packet capture sampling to validate no stale tuples exist.
- Add fuzz test to stress teardown orderings to ensure no race regression.
monitoring:
- Dashboards added: Dedicated > Conntrack Leaks (counts of stale tuples), Per-tenant NAT mismatch alerts, DNS cache hit/miss by tenant. Links: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/conntrack_leaks
- Alerts: fire-critical when >5 conntrack cross-tenant hits in 5m window or >1% of requests see DNS mismatches for a tenant.
- Tracing: add tenant_id tag to netd logs and host NAT traces for correlation.
customer_communications:
- 2026-03-02: initial outreach to impacted customers with explanation and short-term mitigations (guardrail enabled).
- 2026-03-06: status update: hotfix implemented in canary, validation under way.
- 2026-03-13: post-deploy notice: kernel-level fix scheduled, expected full remediation within 2 weeks, SLA credit offer for customers who experienced outages.
- Template messages drafted and approved by Legal: https://drive.redwood.com/communications/dedicated-isolation-incident
postmortem_actions: Document conntrack behavior in Dedicated networking runbook
Add API flag to opt-out of host-NAT optimization per tenant
Create perf regression dashboard when per-namespace conntrack enabled
Schedule kernel patch validation in lab images
notes: Code review pending from kernel infra team (requested reviews from @lin and @marco). Hotfix QA passed on canary hosts with Customer X traffic replay. Need legal approval for SLA credit language before outbound email. Follow-up to automate conntrack teardown on tenant decommission path.
next_steps:
1) Complete kernel infra review and merge runtime patch.
2) Full fleet rollout of netd hotfix if canary shows zero cross-tenant hits for 72h.
3) Open charter for deeper network isolation project to remove reliance on host-level NAT for Dedicated egress.
4) Close ticket after post-deploy monitoring window and customer confirmation.
